h2o-concentration-sign.problem: F3: the H2O initial-concentration polynomial has only positive coefficients, 55.93 M at 25 degC and rising with T, while water density falls with T (about 55.35 M at 25 degC).
h2o-concentration-sign.solution: Trace the coefficients to their source, fix the sign or variable (K vs degC), add a test at 4, 25 and 80 degC, and regenerate goldens with approval.

g-value-dose-rate-range.problem: F2: GValuesBoscolo._scale_factor (variable_GValues) has no valid dose-rate range, no clamp and is inf at 0 Gy/s.
g-value-dose-rate-range.solution: Document the fitted dose-rate range, clamp or raise ValueError outside it and reject non-positive dose rates.

timer-next-off-nan.problem: F4: Timer.time_till_next_OFF returns NaN for continuous timers (period = inf: inf * 0 in _phase).
timer-next-off-nan.solution: Return time - start_time as phase when the period is infinite and add tests for constant and single-pulse timers.

result-persistence-gaps.problem: F7, F8, F6, F12: burst_dose_rates is not persisted to HDF5, reconstruct_reactions ignores use_beam=False, parse_dataset_name uses .strip('.sim') (characters, not suffix), and old files keep a doubled catalase k_value.
result-persistence-gaps.solution: Record use_beam and burst_dose_rates in the json config (optional keys, fallback for old files), pass beam=None to reaction_rates when use_beam is False, use removesuffix('.sim'), and add a format version to handle old enzymatic k_value.

simenv-make-hash.problem: F5: SimEnv.make_hash always raises TypeError (unhashable species_order dict) and hashes repr(frozenset), which depends on PYTHONHASHSEED.
simenv-make-hash.solution: Hash a canonical json serialisation (sort_keys) of parameters and initial concentrations, or remove the unused method.

macro-chunked-golden.problem: F10: no golden output for a chunked run with MacroPulsedBeam.
macro-chunked-golden.solution: Add a short chunked macro run to tests/golden/record_golden.py and compare by label with the existing tolerances.

minor-cleanups.problem: F11, F13, F14: temperature leftovers (iter_*_kvalues default 25 degC, convert_to_config_dict), UnitCell API traps (set_beam LET=None, run_till_max_dose t_span, intervals[-2] IndexError) and ruff format would reformat 34 files.
minor-cleanups.solution: Pass the env temperature in ReactionsList, write polynomial coefficients in convert_to_config_dict, make the UnitCell traps explicit (log/raise), and do one dedicated ruff format commit with .gitattributes line endings.

refresh-example-notebook.problem: Notebook check: examples/notebook_basic_usage.ipynb cell 19 passes max_dose positionally to PulsedBeam.from_dose_rate_peak (it lands in n_pulse; the 10 Gy total matches by coincidence); cells 25 and 27 hold a corrupted µ sign; stored outputs predate the refactor.
refresh-example-notebook.solution: Through the Jupyter MCP tools: use max_dose= in cell 19, fix the µ sign, re-run the notebook and save fresh outputs.

rhs-call-overhead.problem: derive costs 108 us per call and jacobian 349 us (Labarbe: 30 species, 85 k-reactions). The cost is NumPy call overhead (np.ones, concatenate, flatnonzero, broadcast_to, the to_full_molar allocation), not arithmetic; the stoichiometry is only 11% non-zero.
rhs-call-overhead.solution: Precompute index arrays and constant buffers in SimMatrices (depletion columns, the ones row), avoid per-call allocations, try sparse stoichiometry, and benchmark an opt-in compiled backend (numba) behind the same derive/jacobian interface.
rhs-call-overhead.sourceDirection: review the code to highlight (1) area of improvement from efficiency point of view and (2) area of improvement from user usage point of view. restrict usage from jupyter lab notebook

chunked-run-scaling.problem: Each chunk has a fixed cost of about 37 ms. ODEResult.append_sol copies the whole history on every chunk (np.append/hstack, so the cost is quadratic in the number of chunks). dose_rates loops in Python over every time point when the rates are reconstructed, and every ODEResult deep-copies env, beam and matrices. A conventional pulsed linac (~1e4 pulses, 2e4 chunks) runs for minutes.
chunked-run-scaling.solution: Accumulate the chunk arrays in lists and concatenate them lazily, vectorise beam.at for an array of times, share the read-only matrices instead of deep-copying them, and consider merging OFF chunks or capping the points stored per chunk.
chunked-run-scaling.sourceDirection: review the code to highlight (1) area of improvement from efficiency point of view and (2) area of improvement from user usage point of view. restrict usage from jupyter lab notebook

notebook-rich-display.problem: In JupyterLab, UnitCell and ODEResult display as '<... object at 0x...>' and SimEnv as a raw dataclass dump: the notebook gives no view of the species, reactions, beam, LET, temperature or run status.
notebook-rich-display.solution: Add a short __repr__ and a _repr_html_ summary for UnitCell, ODEResult (time span, points, chunks, exec time, success, burst count), SimEnv (species and reaction counts by family) and the beams (dose rate, pulses, max dose, time at max dose).

notebook-quiet-logging.problem: The bundled notebook flow prints 18 INFO lines to stdout, each prefixed with a timestamp and 'radiopyo::INFO::'. tqdm is detected by hand through get_ipython, and a plain run() shows no progress at all.
notebook-quiet-logging.solution: Open decision: should notebooks default to WARNING, or keep INFO with a concise format? Also add a quiet flag or context manager for a run, switch to tqdm.auto, and document rp.set_logging_level in the notebook.

notebook-plot-helpers.problem: Every notebook re-codes the log-time plot, the pH from H3O_plus (in uM) and the unit labels. Neither the beams nor ODEResult offer the cumulative dose versus time, which is needed to plot against dose.
notebook-plot-helpers.solution: Add res.plot(species, ax=None, logx=True), res.pH and res.dose (from a new beam.dose_at(t)), with matplotlib as an optional extra. Open decision: which plot defaults to provide.

simpler-setup-api.problem: Setup traps: (a) the bundled notebook calls PulsedBeam.from_dose_rate_peak(peak, period, on_time, max_dose), so the 4th positional argument is n_pulse; it only works because 1000 x 1e-3 x 10 = 10 Gy. (b) sp.set_initial_cc (mol/L) needs a manual uc.update_env(), or the fixed-species vector is stale. (c) Units are mixed: config in mol/L, results, y0 and atol in uM. (d) set_beam(LET=None) silently reuses the previous LET. (e) res['o2'] raises KeyError without suggestions.
simpler-setup-api.solution: Add uc.set_initial_concentration(label, value, unit=...), which rebuilds the matrices; make the beam factory arguments after on_time keyword-only (with a deprecation warning); warn when the LET is reused; suggest close species labels (difflib) in the KeyError; state units in the docstrings and the repr. Open decision: how long to keep positional compatibility.

parameter-sweep-helper.problem: The typical notebook task is a sweep over dose rate, O2, LET or pulse structure, but each new UnitCell costs seconds (see fast-config-loading), and ResCollection / SimCollection have no driver that fills them.
parameter-sweep-helper.solution: Add uc.copy() (a cheap clone of a parsed cell) and a sweep(param_grid, run_kwargs) that returns a ResCollection plus a tidy DataFrame of chosen outputs (final concentrations, integrals), optionally in parallel with joblib. Open decision: the parameter vocabulary of the grid.

notebook-example-ci.problem: examples/notebook_basic_usage.ipynb is not executed by the tests. It passes max_dose positionally (as n_pulse), uses the old alias names (reactions_involving_product), and has a comment claiming reactions_involving returns tuples, so it can drift without anyone noticing.
notebook-example-ci.solution: Execute the notebook in pytest (nbmake or nbclient, with a short t_span) under a marker, and refresh it to show the recommended API once the other seeds land.
